payload.rationale: The contract resolves YES if the single-decimal published CPI monthly change for November 2026 (released Dec 10, 2026; presumably the seasonally adjusted headline all-items MoM figure) is 0.3% or higher. No current data were supplied, so this is a base-rate judgment. Observed background: through 2024 and 2025, headline monthly CPI prints clustered in the 0.1%–0.4% range, with roughly 40–45% of months printing at 0.3% or above; 2025 prints were lifted somewhat by tariff pass-through into core goods, while shelter disinflation and soft energy pulled the other way. Transfer assumption: if inflation in late 2026 is running near 2.5–3% annualized, the typical monthly print centers around 0.2–0.25%, making 0.2% the modal outcome and 0.3%+ somewhat less than even odds. Energy is the main swing factor for a single month and is unforecastable this far ahead. Reasons the estimate could be too high: continued shelter disinflation, weak demand or falling gasoline in November could produce 0.1–0.2% prints, and November prints have historically often landed at 0.2%. Reasons it could be too low: renewed tariff pass-through, a gasoline or food spike, or a firmer inflation regime in 2026 would shift the distribution so that 0.3%+ becomes the modal outcome; also rounding means a true 0.25% prints as 0.3%. Net estimate around 42%.
limitations: No supplied evidence on 2026 inflation trend, energy prices, tariffs, or recent CPI prints.
Uncertain whether contract uses seasonally adjusted headline CPI; assumed standard SA headline MoM.
Single-month CPI prints are highly noisy; forecast is essentially a base rate.
Possible release delays from government shutdown not assessed.
